ideas.title: Beat the lead foot flat into a sheet
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: Plastic flow you work blow by blow is new physics for the island, and it is something you play with your hands, not a device you leave alone and watch. The copper-wire bending already showed metal keeping its shape, and the J2 FEM with lead's yield typed in may end up a one-material rig.

ideas.title: Roll two sheets into the first lead cell
ideas.critique: This is the core of the big goal. A cell that gets stronger each day you form it is a real reason to come back. Filmed, though, it is another jar of liquid wired up while a thing spins, which is the clay pots and motor payoff again unless the forming itself is what people watch.

ideas.title: Copper-plate the lead foot for a friend
ideas.critique: A secondary current distribution solved on a real mesh, where the anode's position decides where the copper lands, is genuine and the patchy salmon blush could look striking in Hikari. Giving the medal to a friend is decoration, and once the foot is plated there is little left to play.

ideas.title: Tap it and hear what it is
ideas.critique: Modal sound from FEM has been done twice before, with the lantern's notes and the chipped stone, so 'fresh kind: sound' is only half true. What is new is using it across materials and to find cracks by ear: a sorting game with a real payoff. It is a small step on old ground, though.

ideas.title: Pour a medal for each friend
ideas.critique: A mouse-tilted ladle where pouring too slow freezes short and too fast overflows is a good skill to learn, and the blobs that come out wrong are charming. But it is the s170 casting again with friend-shaped moulds, so it adds little that is new.

ideas.title: Hold the ladle in my beak
ideas.critique: A body that shows weight through its pose answers the animation goal directly, and every later tool can use it. The risk is a solver that only handles one ladle and ends up as a canned lean, with the slosh faked as a pendulum.

ideas.title: A cup anemometer that remembers yesterday
ideas.critique: Pebbles as a record of the weather is a lovely readable idea. Even so, it is a device spinning alone in front of a fixed camera, the form the island is drowning in, and the player only reads a pile.

ideas.title: Sled the empty cart down the dune
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Friends shrieking downhill while you steer and brake by ploughing a stick is the most playable and shareable idea here, and it tests the cart's rolling resistance under gravity. It reuses Stuck.cart_step!. The stick brake is the only new mechanism, so it has to feel real.

ideas.title: The tide wipes the beach
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Sand that keeps time is genuinely new: swash moving sediment over a persistent field, seen every day. Racing the tide is a thin goal, and a smoothing pass labelled as sediment transport would make this only a look.

ideas.title: The foot in the south cove at dusk (casting's next step)
ideas.critique: This is polish and a film of what was already built. The mirrored sky in the liquid metal could show off Hikari, but it is a material freezing in front of a close fixed camera, which the island has posted before.
